name: Atadei / Eastern Atadei
catalog_citation: Krauße, Daniel. 2016. A brief grammar of the Eastern Atadei language of Lembata, Indonesia. Linguistik Indonesia 34(2): 113-128. Open-access PDF, ojs.linguistik-indonesia.org article 45/43.

catalog_quote: Vowels are not distinguished by length in Atadei. ... The schwa sound /ə/ can occur word-initially after the inherent glottal stop, in medial position between two consonants or between a vowel and consonant, as well as word-finally in proclitics, such as nĕ ‘he, she, it’. It also occurs in medial position with monosyllabic unstressed words, like tĕk ‘not’. ... Syllables in Atadei are basically CV or CVC, and no word can start with a vowel, as the glottal stop precedes any word-initial vowel. Diphthongs are to be regarded as one vowel (V). The following list illustrates the syllable structure of basic Atadei words: ... CVVC móĕn [ˈmo.ən] ‘yours (sg.)’ CV.CV léma [ˈle.ma] ‘five’ éna [ˈʔe.na] ‘who’ CV.CVC ĕnam [ʔə.ˈnam] ‘six’ ténar [ˈte.nar] ‘boat’ CVC.CV puljua [ˈpul.ɟua̯] ‘twelve’ CV.CV.CV hĕpulò [hə.ˈpu.lɔ] ‘ten’ kikilai [ˈki.ki.lai̯] ‘fingers’ CVC.CVC pultèl [ˈpul.tɛl] ‘thirteen’ kanta…

new_statements.relation_note: Catalog record for Atadei / Eastern Atadei has an empty rule; this is the first placement evidence. It is my tally of the archive transcriptions, not a statement by the collector, hence low confidence. The 200 lama1277-paina forms from Keraf 1978 in the same file carry no stress marks.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The work is a word list, not a description: it states no rule, but every citation form carries a primary-stress mark (522 of 590 forms; 0 secondary marks). Tallying the 395 stress-marked disyllabic words: 219 penultimate vs 176 final. The split is conditioned by the penult vowel: with a full vowel in the penult, 206 penult vs 117 final (final stress mostly on CVC-final words, 88, e.g. keˈdak, raˈjan, laˈtar; 29 open-final, mostly body parts, e.g. maˈta, liˈma, uˈlu); with schwa in the penult, 51 final vs 13 penult (kəˈləm, vəˈdək, əˈnam vs ˈkələm, ˈvətəm). Trisyllables (126): 80 final, 39 penult, 7 antepenult; the final-stressed ones are overwhelmingly kə-/hə- prefixed nouns and -kən/-ən suffixed adjectives (anaˈkən, aluˈhən, kedaˈkən), i.e. stress on the suffix. Four-syllable adjectives in -ən are final (kənatiˈŋan). Best summary: predominantly penultimate, schwa penults skipped in favour of the final, heavy CVC finals and the -(k)ən suffix attract stress; considerable variation, incl. the same word marked both ways (ˈkələm 'sky' vs kəˈləm 'moon').
new_statements.secondary_stress: None marked (no ˌ in any Lerek form). In multi-word entries 151 words carry no stress mark at all (function words and second members, e.g. d͡ʒe 'moon' entry, kaj 'wood'), so the marking is per citation form, not per phrase.
new_statements.exceptions: Not stated by the source. Observed in the marks: 13 schwa-penult words with penultimate stress (ˈkələm 'sky', ˈkəkan 'fog', ˈəmat 'arrow', ˈbəkə 'to fly'); 7 antepenult-stressed trisyllables (ˈnalatən, ˈvuliran, ˈkəvaror, ˈmaləhan); reduplications with two marks (ˈpeta+ˈpeta 'bitter').
new_statements.identity_note: The listed work is the Lerek village variety (LexiRumah lect lama1277-lerek, 'Painara, Lerek', glottocode sout2896, ISO lmf; speakers Bernardus Boli Koban and Helena Helu Lajar, recorded 2015-05-16/17). The same also holds 200 unstressed Painara forms (lama1277-paina) from Keraf 1978. Krauße 2016 describes Eastern Atadei / Atadei Painara proper. Fricke 2019 §3.2.5 describes Central Lembata (Kalikasa), a neighbouring Central Lamaholot language in the same Atadei district, which Fricke and Glottolog keep separate from Atadei Painara.

new_statements.relation_note: Catalog rule is empty; Krauße's transcriptions (Eastern Atadei proper, the same language) point the same way as the Lerek word list: penult unless the penult is schwa. He states no rule, so this is evidence, not a description.
new_statements.rule_in_words: No prose rule; the only stress information is the transcriptions in the syllable table and one aside that monosyllabic function words (tĕk 'not') are unstressed. The transcriptions place stress on the penult when its vowel is full (ˈle.ma, ˈʔe.na, ˈte.nar, ˈkan.tar, kə.ˈlu.rak, hə.ˈpu.lɔ, ˌkə.nə.ˈma.ta) and on the final when the penult is schwa (ʔə.ˈnam); ˈki.ki.lai̯ 'fingers' has initial (antepenult) stress; the compound numeral pulléma has primary stress on pul- and secondary on -le-. Consistent with the Lerek word-list tally and with Fricke's Central Lembata rule.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Marked in two forms only: [ˈpul.ˌle.ma] 'fifteen' (secondary on the second member of the compound) and [ˌkə.nə.ˈma.ta] 'in front of the door' (secondary on the initial schwa syllable).
new_statements.exceptions: kikilai [ˈki.ki.lai̯] 'fingers' stressed on the first of three syllables; monosyllabic function words unstressed. The 'stress' at p. 123 ('seems to put more stress on the pronoun') is emphasis, not word stress.

The same also holds 200 unstressed Painara forms (lama1277-paina) from Keraf 1978. Krauße 2016 describes Eastern Atadei / Atadei Painara proper. Fricke 2019 §3.2.5 describes Central Lembata (Kalikasa), a neighbouring Central Lamaholot language in the same Atadei district, which Fricke and Glottolog keep separate from Atadei Painara.

readall_conflicts: No source states a rule for Atadei Painara itself, and the two direct sources disagree on individual words: Fricke's Lerek list has eˈna 'who' with final stress where Krauße's table has [ˈʔe.na], and the Lerek list itself marks kələm both ways (ˈkələm in 'sky', kəˈləm in 'moon') and shows 117 final-stressed disyllables with a full-vowel penult (36%), far more variation than Fricke's tidy Central Lembata rule would predict; her own remark that stress in Central Lembata 'is not always stable' and the ˈke.dak ~ ke.ˈdak free variation cover the CVC-final cases (88 of the 117) but not the 29 open-final body-part nouns (maˈta, liˈma, uˈlu), which may be possessed/bound forms (Krauße cites bound roots nuh- 'mouth', wul- 'neck') — unverified. The schwa effect is consistent across all three sources (Lerek 80% final after schwa penult; Krauße ʔə.ˈnam; Fricke's rule). The -(k)ən suffixed adjectives with final stress in Lerek (anaˈkən, aluˈhən) are not covered by any source's rule.

sources.quote: For Central Lembata (NOT Atadei): 'the penultimate syllable of the word is stressed, unless the penultimate contains the vowel schwa ... Words with penultimate schwa are stressed at the ultimate syllable, such as /bə.ˈka/'; 'for consonant-final words apparent free variation between penultimate and ultimate stress is found ... [ˈke.dak] ~ [ke.ˈdak] ... tendency to stress heavy final syllables'; trisyllabic stems with final identical-vowel sequences surface with final stress and length ([tuˈluː]). No stress statement is made for Atadei Painara; it is cited only via Krauße 2016 and Fricke's 2015

sources.note: Prose stress rule (pp.49-50) for the closest described sister variety (Central Lembata: penultimate unless schwa penult; heavy-final variation) — useful as a family-level caution note on the record, not as a source for Atadei itself.
